correctness.rationale: A complete nonalgebraic singleton type in the generic pair of independent linear orders is uniquely identified by its two insertion gaps. Its disagreement grade is the Hamming size of the symmetric difference of the parameter initial segments. The exact independent rectangle formula d=i+j-2R yields an alternative computation. The supplied C++17 verifier enumerates all 4,037,913 permutations of orders one through ten, compares both complete histograms for every permutation, verifies exact multinomial totals, detects 0 failures through length nine and exactly 32 at length ten, and proves equality of all 32 failures to five generated pair-order symmetry orbits. The explicit witness histogram has a 20,19,20 valley; the all-order persistence is an analytic identity from new border gap pairs and does not rely on extending the finite experiment. The proof states all quantifiers, domain bounds, and the plateau-allowing unimodality definition. No external independent audit is claimed.

originality.rationale: The Fraïssé generic permutation context is in Cameron (2002), while Brignall–Ruškuc–Vatter study simple-extension size, not the joint two-insertion-gap distance histogram. Individually sharp grade bounds, mean grade coefficients, and analogous permutation disagreement measures do not prove unimodality or classify its failure because correlations between grade counts remain unspecified. Searches for the Boolean-lattice maximal-chain distance-enumerator reformulation, two-order one-point extensions, gap-grid histogram unimodality, and exact 32 ten-point exceptions located no decisive prior equivalence. This is best-knowledge priority only; the unindexed-table risk remains explicit.

value.rationale: A total of (n+1)^2 ordered singleton types is independent of the base permutation, so the grade histogram is a natural finer invariant measuring disagreement of the two linear orders. The first failure of unimodality is a nontrivial global shape boundary not forced by pointwise coefficient bounds. A complete 32-element, five-symmetry-orbit minimal classification is mathematically informative even though its finite part uses exhaustive computation; the direct append lemma shows the obstruction persists at every greater order. This is a precise motivated finite cutoff plus infinite structural extension, not a routine restatement of the count or a cherry-picked arbitrary numerical slice.
